raw_case_text:
Congenital brucellosis was diagnosed in patients 1 and 2, who were 3-month-old twins (Technical Appendix Table). They were prematurely delivered by cesarean section on July 6, 2012, at the Provincial Maternity and Child Care Center (Guangzhou, China). The boy (patient 1, Apgar score 9-10/1-10 min) had a birthweight of 2.3 kg, and the girl (patient 2, Apgar score 9-10/1-10 min) had a birthweight of 1.8 kg. They received standard care for preterm neonates at the hospital. They were discharged once their weight reached 2.5 kg; this happened for patient 1 at 3 weeks of age and for patient 2 at 4 weeks of age (July 29 and August 3, 2012, respectively).
On October 2, 2012, the boy was examined at the hospital for irregular fever up to 39 C. On October 9, he was readmitted to the hospital with a fever of 38 C and weight of 5.0 kg. Chest radiograph showed signs of increased bronchovascular shadows. Mezlocillin sodium and sulbactam sodium (4:1) and ribavirin were administered, but the patient did not improve. On the same day, the girl had a cough and low-level fever (37-37.5 C) but was not hospitalized. On October 16, B. melitensis was isolated from a blood culture from patient 1, in whom brucellosis with alveobronchiolitis, abnormal hepatic function, and moderate anemia were initially diagnosed when he was 3 months and 10 days of age.
On October 17, the twins were transferred to an infectious disease hospital, where they had extensive physical and laboratory examinations (Table 1). During 57 days of hospitalization, the boy received general and specific therapies for brucellosis. Brucellosis and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency were diagnosed in the girl, and she received appropriate treatment. At the time of discharge (December 12), the twins were well and without fever. They left the hospital for home care, which was supervised by a local general practitioner who provided rifampin and sulfamethoxazole for up to 6 weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 3-month-old preterm male twin (Patient 1) presented on October 2, 2012, with irregular fevers up to 39 C, while his twin sister (Patient 2) developed cough and low-grade fever (37.0-37.5 C) on October 9, 2012.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Three-month-old twins delivered prematurely at 34+2 weeks' gestation by cesarean section on July 6, 2012, due to premature rupture of membranes and maternal phase I chorioamnionitis (discharged at 3 and 4 weeks of age once reaching 2.5 kg) developed febrile illness in early October 2012. The male twin (Patient 1) presented on October 2, 2012, with irregular fevers up to 39 C and was readmitted on October 9 (temperature 38 C, weight 5.0 kg), failing empiric mezlocillin-sulbactam and ribavirin; his twin sister (Patient 2) developed cough and low-grade fever (37-37.5 C) on October 9, and both were transferred to an infectious disease hospital on October 17, 2012.
subjective.past_medical_history: Preterm twins born at 34+2 weeks' gestation via cesarean section (birthweight 2.3 kg for boy, 1.8 kg for girl; Apgar 9-10) to a mother with chorioamnionitis and undiagnosed brucellosis; glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency diagnosed in the female twin.
subjective.review_of_systems: Boy (Patient 1): Positive for irregular fever up to 39 C. Girl (Patient 2): Positive for cough and low-grade fever (37-37.5 C).

objective.physical_examination: Patient 1 on October 9 readmission: temperature 38.0 C, weight 5.0 kg. Patient 2: low-grade fever (37.0-37.5 C).
objective.routine_investigations: Patient 1: moderate anemia, abnormal liver function tests, and chest radiograph showing increased bronchovascular markings consistent with alveobronchiolitis. Patient 2: diagnosed with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
objective.advanced_workup: Quantitative PCR and abbreviated AMOS PCR of blood culture isolates identified Brucella melitensis biotype 3; 16-locus multilocus variable-number tandem repeat analysis (MLVA-16: 1-5-3-13-2-3-3-2-6-22-9-6-9-11-4-5) confirmed identical genotypes between both twins and their mother.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Blood cultures from both twins grew Brucella melitensis biotype 3, serum standard tube agglutination titers were 1:400 in both twins (declining to 1:200 on follow-up), and archived cord blood plasma was Rose Bengal positive, confirming congenital Brucella melitensis biotype 3 infection in preterm twins. Following a 57-day hospitalization with targeted anti-Brucella therapy, repeat blood cultures on November 18 and 29 were sterile, and the twins were discharged afebrile on December 12, 2012, to complete up to 6 weeks of outpatient oral rifampin and sulfamethoxazole.
